pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can respond to texts correctly for comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional.
4. Show that you can: create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read texts of up to 500 words related to the selected theme,

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places?
2. How can we predict what will happen in a text or story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
